I've been working this land since I was little — watching my mother, then doing it myself. Ten mu is all we have, and my husband and eldest son go out to work in the city most of the year, so I manage most of the farm work myself, with help during busy seasons. I don't read much, but I know this soil. I follow what my neighbors do and what my own eyes tell me.

This land runs wheat in winter, maize in summer — same ground, back to back, every year. That's how it's always been done here in Quzhou. I won't change that.

**Wheat:** I'll plant in mid-October after the maize comes off. I'll buy the improved wheat seeds from the village supply station — same kind I used last two years, good germination, reliable. Before planting I'll do a rotary tillage pass to break up the maize stubble. I put base fertilizer down at planting — diammonium phosphate and some urea mixed in. Then I top-dress nitrogen at jointing. I irrigate at jointing, heading, and grain-fill — three times total, pulling from the well. Two pesticide sprays: one herbicide in early spring, one for powdery mildew and aphids before heading. I expect around 450 jin per mu — that's a normal year for us here.

**Maize:** Right after wheat harvest in June I get the seed in fast — no time to waste, the season is short. I use hybrid seed, everyone does now, it's not expensive and the yield is much better than the old types. I do a quick rotary pass or sometimes plant straight into the stubble if it's already chopped by the combine. Fertilizer goes in at planting and again when the plant is knee-high. Summer rains help but I irrigate once or twice depending on how dry it gets. Two pesticide sprays — one for fall armyworm or corn borer, one as needed. I expect around 550 jin per mu in a decent year.
